title: Architecture and Standards: API, Infra, Observability, Model-Serving Guidelines and ADRs
author: Ava Mitchell
content:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. It also enumerates active Decision Records (ADRs) that shape current platform behavior. The guidance below is intended for new and existing services, SDKs, the hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to any service or repo owned by engineering that: provides customer-facing HTTP/SDK APIs, runs model-serving infrastructure, or emits production telemetry.
- Not a replacement for team-level runbooks; it is the company-wide baseline for design, security posture, and operability.

Principles (short):
1. Production-first: prioritize predictable latency, reliability, and clear SLOs.
2. Developer ergonomics: standards should be automatable and enforced by CI.
3. Observability by default: metrics, structured logs, and traces required.
4. Secure-by-default: least-privilege, encrypted secrets, and audit logs.
5. Backward-compatible evolution: versioning and gradual rollouts minimize customer disruption.

1) API Standards
- API contract: All public and partner-facing endpoints must include an OpenAPI v3 spec stored in the repo at /api/openapi.yaml and published to the internal API gateway catalog.
- Versioning: Use path versioning (e.g., /v1/..., /v2/...) for breaking changes. Deprecation schedule: 90 days notice for major versions; document migration guides.
- Schema design: Prefer explicit request/response schemas; avoid ad-hoc fields. Use JSON Schema for validation at the edge.
- Authentication & authorization: OAuth2 (service-to-service via JWTs) for internal services; API key + token binding for customer/hosted API. All token validation should be centralized in auth-library.
- Pagination & filtering: Cursor-based pagination for list endpoints (limit, cursor). Avoid offset-based pagination on large result sets.
- Error handling: Standardize on JSON problem details (RFC7807). Error object must include: type, title, status, trace_id, and optional user_facing_message. Map all 5xx errors to SRE alert categories.
- Rate limiting: Per-customer rate limiting enforced at API gateway with documented quotas; implement graceful 429 responses with Retry-After.
- Streaming: Use chunked-transfer/HTTP streaming or websocket for long-lived generations. Provide content-type application/x-ndjson for line-delimited event streams.
- OpenAPI example (partial):
  paths:
    /v1/generate:
      post:
        summary: Text generation endpoint
        requestBody:
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerationRequest'

2) Coding Standards
- Languages and frameworks: Primary service languages are Go (backend infra), TypeScript (frontend and Node.js services), and Python (inference pipelines and evals). Use the language-specific linting rules below.
- Linting & formatting: Enforce gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, ESLint + Prettier for TypeScript, Black + Flake8 for Python. CI must fail on lint/format violations.
- Testing: 80%+ unit coverage encouraged for core logic; integration tests required for external dependencies. Use testcontainers or equivalent for infra-focused integration tests.
- Dependency management: Use dependabot or Renovate with weekly PR cadence for non-critical updates, immediate attention for security fixes.
- PRs & code reviews: Small, focused PRs; include design notes for non-trivial changes. Two approvers required for infra and runtime changes; at least one reviewer from eng-platform or eng-serving-runtime for model-serving changes.
- Secret handling: Never store secrets in repo. Use KMS + vault patterns defined in infra standards.

3) Infrastructure Standards (IaC, networking, deployment)
- IaC: All infra must be defined in Terraform modules stored under /infra. Modules must be versioned and consumed from the central registry (git tags). No ad-hoc cloud console changes without a follow-up PR.
- Environments: enforce three canonical environments: dev (short-lived), staging (mirror of prod with sampling), prod. Use separate cloud accounts and network boundaries per environment.
- Naming conventions: resource names must start with company shortname rdinf-<team>-<svc>-<env>-<component>. Document exceptions in the exceptions tracker.
- Secrets & keys: Use customer-managed KMS for production keys; secrets in HashiCorp Vault with RBAC policies. Rotate root-level credentials quarterly.
- Networking: VPC CIDR allocation is coordinated by eng-infra. Private subnets for model-serving pools; egress restricted by default. Public endpoints go through API gateway + WAF.
- Autoscaling & capacity: Define autoscaling policies with safe min/max bounds. For Dedicated GPU pools, implement buffer capacity = steady-state QPS * 1.25 or min 2 GPUs.

4) Model-Serving Standards
- Model artifacts: Standardize artifacts as OCI-style bundles with metadata.json including: model_version, param_count, tokenizer_spec, quantization_profile, expected_vram. Store in artifact registry with immutable tags.
- Packaging: Provide a model manifest with inference config (batching, max_seq_len, kv_cache_support). Include a signed checksum and provenance fields (source, checksum, created_by).
- Quantization profiles: Maintain curated quantization profiles in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Each profile must have measured perf/cost deltas and sample quality regressions.
- Runtime compatibility: Runtime must clearly declare supported ops and acceptable operator fallbacks. Backwards compatibility matrix should be automated in CI per release.
- Rollouts: Canary -> progressive rollout -> full. Canary size default 1% traffic for new model families, increase to 10% after 24h if error/quality metrics stable. Use canary control plane to pin model variants.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: On performance anomalies, automatically route to a validated fallback model with equivalent schema. Document fallback mappings in model registry.
- Caching & batching: Support prefix/KV cache and dynamic batching. Batch-size selection should be telemetry-driven with fallback to single-request mode for latency-sensitive routes.
- Model validation: Run eval harness and a suite of regression tests (quality prompts and perf microbenchmarks) before production rollout. Record eval results in model-onboarding.

5) Observability Standards
- Three pillars: metrics, logs, traces. Every service must emit:
  - Metrics: service_request_count, service_request_latency_seconds (histogram), service_error_count, model_inference_tokens_total where applicable.
  - Structured logs: JSON logs with fields: ts, level, message, service, env, trace_id, span_id, request_id, user_id (if available), error_code.
  - Distributed tracing: All cross-service requests include W3C traceparent header and propagate trace_id.
- Metric naming and tags: Follow the pattern rdinf.<team>.<service>.<metric>. Use stable label keys: env, region, model_version, route, customer_id (hashed).
- Dashboards: Per-service dashboards must include: QPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depths, and per-model quality regressions where applicable.
- Alerts: Alerting thresholds are tied to SLOs. Primary alerts: sustained p99 latency breach (>3x target for 5m), error rate > 0.5% for 5m, GPU OOM events, or queue depth > configured threshold. Pager schedule must be attached to critical alerts.
- Logging retention: Structured logs retained 30 days by default; extended retention is an add-on. Audit logs are retained 1 year.

6) Performance Standards and SLOs
- Canonical SLO guidance (examples):
  Service Type | Route class | p95 latency target | p99 latency target | error budget/month
  Hosted generation (standard) | /v1/generate (short) | 200 ms | 800 ms | 0.5%
  Hosted generation (long) | /v1/generate (streaming) | 1.5 s | 5 s | 1.0%
  Embeddings | /v1/embeddings | 100 ms | 300 ms | 0.5%
  Management APIs | /v1/models | 200 ms | 1 s | 0.2%
- Capacity planning: Run weekly autoscaling simulations and monthly stress tests. For GPU fleets, measure tokens/sec per GPU at 4, 8, 16 batch sizes for common model families and maintain a published performance matrix.
- Benchmarking: Use the benchmarking-and-perf-suite in eng-serving-runtime. All model admissions to prod must include p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token baselines.

7) ADRs (Decision Records)
- ADR-2025-01: Runtime kernel selection (2025-03-10) - We adopted dynamic kernel chooser that selects kernels by model architecture and sequence length. Owner: Marcus Lee. Link: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-2025-01-runtime-kernel-selection.
- ADR-2025-09: Default quantization strategy (2025-11-02) - Adopted per-model-profile quantization with validation harness; default: 8-bit GPTQ for large decoder-only models. Owner: Priya Nair. Link: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/adr-2025-09-quantization.
- ADR-2026-02: API versioning policy (2026-02-15) - Path-based versioning adopted; deprecation policy standardized at 90 days. Owner: Ava Mitchell. Link: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-2026-02-api-versioning.
- ADR-2026-07: Observability signal definitions (2026-07-20) - Standardized metric names and labels; mandated histogram buckets for latency. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Link: /confluence/eng-sre/adr-2026-07-observability-signals.

8) Adoption checklist (for new services or major changes)
1. Create OpenAPI spec and place at /api/openapi.yaml.
2. Add CI linting/formatting checks and unit tests.
3. Add IaC changes via terraform module and run plan in staging.
4. Implement metrics/logs/traces with canonical names.
5. Define SLOs and add to SLO dashboard.
6. Prepare rollout plan (canary percentage, rollback criteria) and safety limits.
7. Notify SRE and Platform teams and schedule a canary window.
8. Run model evals and perf benchmarks (if model-serving).
9. Add documentation page and link to product docs and release notes.

9) Exceptions and change process
- To deviate from these standards, submit an ADR with technical justification, owner, rollout plan, and compensating controls. Exceptions are reviewed monthly by a standing Architecture Council (eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre). Temporary exceptions must include an expiry and an owner.

Appendix: Example SLO YAML snippet
  name: host.generate.p95
  service: host-api
  objective: "0.95 <= 200ms"
  window: 30d
  tags: ["api","generate","production"]

Owners:
- Standards author: Ava Mitchell (architecture-and-standards working group).
- Ongoing maintenance: eng-platform (standards doc updates), eng-sre (SLO/alerting), eng-serving-runtime (model-serving specifics).

Related work and references:
- Model onboarding checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding
- Quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles
- Runtime architecture: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture

Contact and review cadence:
- Standards review: quarterly. Submit issues or update requests via the architecture-and-standards GitHub board.
- For urgent changes, tag architecture@redwood-inference.internal and schedule a review with the Architecture Council.

This page is authoritative for cross-team architecture decisions and should be referenced in PR templates, runbooks, and onboarding material.
